# Market failures and the environment

<html><div style='float:left'></div><hr color='#EB811B' size=1px width=796px></html>


<!-- --- -->

<!-- # The ideal world: mathematical -->

<!-- In the best case scenario, a market equilibrium leads to the efficient allocation -->

<!-- -- -->

<!-- Example: bread -->

<!-- -- -->

<!-- Household gets utility $U(B,C)$ from consuming bread $B$ and electricity $C$ -->

<!-- -- -->

<!-- Price of bread is $p_b$, price of electricity is $p_e$, household has a budget $Y$ -->

<!-- -- -->

<!-- Household solves: -->
<!-- \begin{align} -->
<!--   &\max_{B,E} U(B,E) \quad \text{subject to: } \quad p_b B + p_e E = Y \\ -->
<!--   &\max_{B} U\left(B,\frac{Y - p_b B}{p_e}\right) -->
<!-- \end{align} -->

<!-- --- -->

<!-- # The ideal world: mathematical -->

<!-- \begin{align} -->
<!--   \max_{B} U\left(B,\frac{Y - p_b B}{p_e}\right) -->
<!-- \end{align} -->

<!-- The first-order condition gives us what defines the utility maximizing choice of bread: -->
<!-- $$\frac{\partial U\left(B,\frac{Y - p_b B}{p_e}\right)}{\partial B} + \frac{\partial U\left(B,\frac{Y - p_b B}{p_e}\right)}{\partial E}\left(- \frac{p_b}{p_e} \right) = 0$$ -->

<!-- $$\frac{\partial U\left(B,\frac{Y - p_b B}{p_e}\right)}{\partial B} \Bigg/\frac{\partial U\left(B,\frac{Y - p_b B}{p_e}\right)}{\partial E}= \frac{p_b}{p_e}$$ -->

<!-- --- -->

<!-- # The ideal world: mathematical -->


<!-- $$\frac{\partial U\left(B,\frac{Y - p_b B}{p_c}\right)}{\partial B} \Bigg/\frac{\partial U\left(B,\frac{Y - p_b B}{p_c}\right)}{\partial C}= \frac{p_b}{p_c}$$ -->
<!-- .hi[Left hand side:] marginal rate of substitution (slope of indifference curve between bread and electricity) -->

<!-- .hi[Right hand side:] relative prices (slope of budget constraint) -->

<!-- -- -->

<!-- Households consume the bundle of goods that makes their indifference curve tangent to the budget constraint -->

# The ideal world: graphical

In the best case scenario, a market equilibrium leads to the efficient allocation

--

Example: bread

--

We have a private bread supply curve (private MC)

--

We have a private bread demand curve (private MB)

--

In equilibrium: supply = demand so PMC = PMB = price

--

For bread, the private costs and benefits are very likely the social costs and benefits

.pull-left[
```{r pmb-pmb, echo = FALSE, fig.show = 'hide', warning = F}
supply <- function(x) 5 + 0.5*x
demand <- function(x) 30 - x
cs_points <- tibble(x = c(0, 16.67, 0),
                     y = c(13.33, 13.33, 30))
ps_points <- tibble(x = c(0, 16.67, 0),
                     y = c(13.33, 13.33, 5))
ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = cs_points, aes(x = x, y = y), fill = "red", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_polygon(data = ps_points, aes(x = x, y = y), fill = "blue", alpha = 0.2) +
  annotate("text", x = 26, y = 22, label = "PMC=SMC", size = 8) +
  annotate("text", x = 27, y = 10, label = "PMB=SMB", size = 8) +
  stat_function(fun = demand, color = "#ca5670", size = 1.5) +
  stat_function(fun = supply, color = "#638ccc", size = 1.5) +
  annotate("segment", x = 0, xend = 16.67, y = 13.33, yend = 13.33,
           linetype = "dashed", size = 1.5, color = "grey50") +
  annotate("segment", x = 16.67, xend = 16.67, y = 0, yend = 13.33,
           linetype = "dashed", size = 1.5, color = "grey50") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    title = element_text(size = 24),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 24), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 24),

    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#ffffff",colour = NA),

  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(labels = expression(P^'*'), breaks = c(13.33), limits = c(0,30)) +
  labs(x = "Quantity",
       y = "Price") 

```

# Externalities

<html><div style='float:left'></div><hr color='#EB811B' size=1px width=796px></html>

---

# Externalities

If the world consisted only of competitive markets, private goods, and no third parties, there would be no reason to do anything after Econ 101

--

That's not the case in the real world

--

In the real world we have .hi-blue[externalities]

> An externality exists whenever an individual or firm undertakes an action that impacts another individual or firm in an unintended way for which the latter is not compensated (a negative externality), or for which the latter does not pay (a positive externality)

---

# Externalities

What is the problem with externalities for market outcomes and efficiency?

--

There is not a market for the externality

--

E.g. at Wegmans or Agway you will not find some important goods on sale:
--

- Cleaner air outside
--

- Biodiversity in the Amazon

--

The central problem is that there are goods that are .hi-red[not priced], why is this a problem?

--

Markets rely on prices to signal the social value of goods

---

# Arizona's water problems share a market-failure structure

.pull-left[
.hi[Colorado River]

- Arizona shares a limited river supply with other states, Tribal Nations, and Mexico
- Each user's withdrawal increases scarcity for other users
]

.pull-right[
.hi[Groundwater]

- Pumping from a shared aquifer lowers the water table and can cause land subsidence
- Pumpers do not bear all the costs imposed on nearby wells and future users
]

.hi[Both:] incomplete property rights + missing prices + high transaction costs

---

# Colorado River rules are being rewritten for 2027

```{r, echo = FALSE}
local_video("videos/02-market-failures-colorado-river-2026.mp4")
```

---

# The post-2026 Colorado River regime is not yet settled

As of August 26, 2026:

- Current operating guidelines and drought plans expire at the end of 2026
- The July 31 final environmental impact statement identifies an adaptive framework through 2036
- The Department of the Interior expects final guidelines before October 1

.hi[The economic question:] who bears shortages when river flows are uncertain?

<!-- Sources:
- Bureau of Reclamation, post-2026 operations: https://www.usbr.gov/ColoradoRiverBasin/post2026/index.html (accessed August 26, 2026)
-->

---

# Saudi farming exposed Arizona groundwater rules

```{r, echo = FALSE}
local_video("videos/02-market-failures-arizona-water.mp4")
```

<!-- Sources:
- CBS Mornings, "Arizona Water Controversy": https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b78owYAd0iw
-->

---

# Arizona has begun regulating Ranegras groundwater

- Annual withdrawals have exceeded natural recharge by roughly .hi-red[900%]
- One monitored well has fallen more than .hi-red[240 feet] since the 1980s, and groundwater loss has caused land subsidence
- Arizona designated Ranegras Plain as its eighth Active Management Area in January 2026
- The new rules restrict irrigation on new acreage and require large users to measure and report pumping

.hi[The change:] an open-access aquifer is becoming a managed common-pool resource

<!-- Sources:
- Arizona Department of Water Resources, January 15, 2026: https://www.azwater.gov/news/articles/2026-01-14
-->

---

# Groundwater scarcity is also moving through the courts

- Arizona sued Fondomonte in December 2024, alleging that excessive pumping threatened nearby communities and infrastructure
- In February 2026, the attorney general argued that the new Active Management Area complements rather than replaces the lawsuit
- The state is seeking remedies targeted at the alleged harm, while the Active Management Area regulates pumping throughout the basin

.hi[Same externality, different tools:] basin-wide regulation and liability for alleged harm

<!-- Sources:
- Arizona Attorney General, February 3, 2026: https://www.azag.gov/press-release/attorney-general-mayes-continues-lawsuit-against-fondomonte-violating-public-nuisance
-->

---

# Groundwater enforcement now uses settlements as well as lawsuits

```{r, echo = FALSE}
local_video("videos/02-market-failures-groundwater-lawsuit-2026.mp4")
```

# Externalities: several classifications

We can classify externalities in a few ways:

--

.hi[Production externalities:] 
--
generated by a firm in the process of producing some output (e.g. pollution, innovation)

--

.hi[Consumption externalities:] 
--
generated by an individual in the process of consuming an output (e.g. congestion, vaccination)

--

.hi-red[Negative externalities:] 
--
imposes external **costs** (e.g. pollution)

--

.hi-blue[Positive externalities:] 
--
imposes external **benefits** (e.g. vaccination)

---

# Positive externalities: graphical

.pull-left[
```{r pos-ext0, echo = FALSE, fig.show = 'hide', warning = F}
pmc <- function(x) 5 + 0.5*x
smb <- function(x) 40 - x
pmb <- function(x) 30 - x
ggplot() +
  annotate("text", x = 26, y = 21, label = "SMC=PMC", size = 8) +
```

# Vaccination and infection create externalities

.hi-blue[Vaccination can create a positive externality:]

- It lowers an individual's probability of infection
- When it also lowers transmission, it protects other people

--

.hi-red[Infection can create a negative externality:]

- Exposure shifts uncompensated risk to other people
- Private choices omit some expected health costs

--

.hi[Efficiency:] private choices use PMB and PMC; social choices use SMB and SMC

---

# Why do externalities arise?

Typically one of two reasons:

--

1. Poorly defined property rights
  - Who owns the right to the air?
--

2. High transactions costs
  - Hard to bargain over desired air quality with millions of people


Let's conceptualize a model of efficient bargaining using an Edgeworth Box

---

# Why do externalities arise? Edgeworth Box

- Two individuals: A and B
- Two private goods: X and Y

Each individual begins with an initial endowment of each good:
- $A: w_X^A, w_Y^A$
- $B: w_X^B, w_Y^B$

This gives us a total endowment:
- $W_X = w_X^A + w_X^B$
- $W_Y = w_Y^A + w_Y^B$


---

# Why do externalities arise? Edgeworth Box

Each person starts with an ordinary consumption diagram

Rotate B's diagram 180 degrees and place it over A's so the endowment points coincide

The result is a box with width $W_X$ and height $W_Y$

<center>
```{r edgeworth1-panels, echo = FALSE, fig.show = 'hide', warning = F, fig.width = 9.5, fig.height = 5.2}
# Apply the deck's common figure style, with axes shown only for the two
# ordinary individual diagrams.
edgeworth_theme = function(base_size = 18, show_axes = FALSE) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#ffffff", colour = NA),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#ffffff", colour = NA),
      axis.line = if (show_axes) element_line(colour = "black") else element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      axis.title = if (show_axes) element_text(size = 20) else element_blank(),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 21, hjust = 0.5),
      plot.margin = margin(28, 42, 34, 42)
    )
}

edgeworth1_total_x = 10
edgeworth1_total_y = 8
edgeworth1_endowment = c(x = 6.4, y = 2.4)
edgeworth1_optimum = c(x = 4.7, y = 3.76)

edgeworth1_utility_a = function(x, y) sqrt(x * y)
edgeworth1_utility_b = function(x, y) {
  sqrt((edgeworth1_total_x - x) * (edgeworth1_total_y - y))
}
edgeworth1_mrs_a = function(x, y) y / x
edgeworth1_mrs_b = function(x, y) {
  (edgeworth1_total_y - y) / (edgeworth1_total_x - x)
}
edgeworth1_contract_y = function(x) {
  edgeworth1_total_y / edgeworth1_total_x * x
}

edgeworth1_initial_utility_a = edgeworth1_utility_a(
  edgeworth1_endowment["x"], edgeworth1_endowment["y"]
)
edgeworth1_initial_utility_b = edgeworth1_utility_b(
  edgeworth1_endowment["x"], edgeworth1_endowment["y"]
)
edgeworth1_optimal_utility_a = edgeworth1_utility_a(
  edgeworth1_optimum["x"], edgeworth1_optimum["y"]
)
edgeworth1_optimal_utility_b = edgeworth1_utility_b(
  edgeworth1_optimum["x"], edgeworth1_optimum["y"]
)

edgeworth1_curve_x = seq(0.05, edgeworth1_total_x - 0.05, length.out = 1200)
edgeworth1_initial_curves = bind_rows(
  tibble(
    x = edgeworth1_curve_x,
    y = edgeworth1_initial_utility_a^2 / x,
    agent = "A"
  ),
  tibble(
    x = edgeworth1_curve_x,
    y = edgeworth1_total_y - edgeworth1_initial_utility_b^2 /
      (edgeworth1_total_x - x),
    agent = "B"
  )
) |>
  filter(dplyr::between(y, 0, edgeworth1_total_y))
edgeworth1_optimal_curves = bind_rows(
  tibble(
    x = edgeworth1_curve_x,
    y = edgeworth1_optimal_utility_a^2 / x,
    agent = "A"
  ),
  tibble(
    x = edgeworth1_curve_x,
    y = edgeworth1_total_y - edgeworth1_optimal_utility_b^2 /
      (edgeworth1_total_x - x),
    agent = "B"
  )
) |>
  filter(dplyr::between(y, 0, edgeworth1_total_y))
edgeworth1_lens = tibble(
  x = edgeworth1_curve_x,
  y_a = edgeworth1_initial_utility_a^2 / x,
  y_b = edgeworth1_total_y - edgeworth1_initial_utility_b^2 /
    (edgeworth1_total_x - x)
) |>
  filter(
    dplyr::between(y_a, 0, edgeworth1_total_y),
    dplyr::between(y_b, 0, edgeworth1_total_y),
    y_a <= y_b
  )
edgeworth1_contract_start = sqrt(
  edgeworth1_initial_utility_a^2 /
    (edgeworth1_total_y / edgeworth1_total_x)
)
edgeworth1_contract_end = edgeworth1_total_x - sqrt(
  edgeworth1_initial_utility_b^2 /
    (edgeworth1_total_y / edgeworth1_total_x)
)
edgeworth1_pareto_set = tibble(
  x = seq(
    edgeworth1_contract_start,
    edgeworth1_contract_end,
    length.out = 300
  )
) |>
  mutate(y = edgeworth1_contract_y(x))
edgeworth1_trace_points = tibble(
  point_id = 1:2,
  x = c(4.45, 4.92)
) |>
  mutate(y = edgeworth1_contract_y(x))
edgeworth1_trace_curves = purrr::pmap_dfr(
  edgeworth1_trace_points,
  function(point_id, x, y) {
    utility_a_squared = x * y
    utility_b_squared = (edgeworth1_total_x - x) *
      (edgeworth1_total_y - y)
    arc_x = seq(x - 1.15, x + 1.15, length.out = 220)

    bind_rows(
      tibble(
        point_id = point_id,
        x = arc_x,
        y = utility_a_squared / arc_x,
        agent = "A"
      ),
      tibble(
        point_id = point_id,
        x = arc_x,
        y = edgeworth1_total_y - utility_b_squared /
          (edgeworth1_total_x - arc_x),
        agent = "B"
      )
    ) |>
      filter(dplyr::between(y, 0, edgeworth1_total_y))
  }
)

# The efficient allocation is on the contract curve and strictly improves
# both agents' utility relative to the initial endowment. The thick Pareto-set
# segment contains exactly the efficient allocations that also improve on it.
stopifnot(
  edgeworth1_optimal_utility_a > edgeworth1_initial_utility_a,
  edgeworth1_optimal_utility_b > edgeworth1_initial_utility_b,
  abs(
    edgeworth1_mrs_a(edgeworth1_optimum["x"], edgeworth1_optimum["y"]) -
      edgeworth1_mrs_b(edgeworth1_optimum["x"], edgeworth1_optimum["y"])
  ) < 1e-10,
  edgeworth1_contract_start < edgeworth1_optimum["x"],
  edgeworth1_contract_end > edgeworth1_optimum["x"],
  all(dplyr::between(
    edgeworth1_trace_points$x,
    edgeworth1_contract_start,
    edgeworth1_contract_end
  )),
  max(abs(
    edgeworth1_mrs_a(edgeworth1_trace_points$x, edgeworth1_trace_points$y) -
      edgeworth1_mrs_b(edgeworth1_trace_points$x, edgeworth1_trace_points$y)
  )) < 1e-10,
  all(
    edgeworth1_utility_a(edgeworth1_trace_points$x, edgeworth1_trace_points$y) >=
      edgeworth1_initial_utility_a - 1e-10
  ),
  all(
    edgeworth1_utility_b(edgeworth1_trace_points$x, edgeworth1_trace_points$y) >=
      edgeworth1_initial_utility_b - 1e-10
  ),
  max(abs(
    edgeworth1_mrs_a(edgeworth1_pareto_set$x, edgeworth1_pareto_set$y) -
      edgeworth1_mrs_b(edgeworth1_pareto_set$x, edgeworth1_pareto_set$y)
  )) < 1e-10,
  all(
    edgeworth1_utility_a(edgeworth1_pareto_set$x, edgeworth1_pareto_set$y) >=
      edgeworth1_initial_utility_a - 1e-10
  ),
  all(
    edgeworth1_utility_b(edgeworth1_pareto_set$x, edgeworth1_pareto_set$y) >=
      edgeworth1_initial_utility_b - 1e-10
  )
)

# Draw the standard box. Each later option adds the next economic object while
# preserving the geometry shown in the earlier stage.
draw_edgeworth_box = function(
  show_panels = FALSE,
  show_lens = FALSE,
  show_optimum = FALSE,
  additional_tangencies = 0L,
  show_pareto_set = FALSE
) {
  if (show_panels) {
    panel_endowments = list(
      A = c(
        x = unname(edgeworth1_endowment["x"]),
        y = unname(edgeworth1_endowment["y"])
      ),
      B = c(
        x = unname(edgeworth1_total_x - edgeworth1_endowment["x"]),
        y = unname(edgeworth1_total_y - edgeworth1_endowment["y"])
      )
    )
    panel_colors = c(A = "#ca5670", B = "#638ccc")

    panel_plots = purrr::imap(
      panel_endowments,
      function(endowment, agent) {
        utility = sqrt(endowment["x"] * endowment["y"])
        curve = tibble(
          x = edgeworth1_curve_x,
          y = utility^2 / edgeworth1_curve_x
        ) |>
          filter(dplyr::between(y, 0, edgeworth1_total_y))

        ggplot(curve, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
          annotate(
            "segment", x = endowment["x"], xend = endowment["x"],
            y = 0, yend = edgeworth1_total_y,
            linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1, color = "grey50"
          ) +
          annotate(
            "segment", x = 0, xend = edgeworth1_total_x,
            y = endowment["y"], yend = endowment["y"],
            linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1, color = "grey50"
          ) +
          geom_line(color = panel_colors[agent], linewidth = 1.6) +
          annotate(
            "point", x = endowment["x"], y = endowment["y"],
            shape = 21, size = 5.2, stroke = 1.4,
            fill = "white", color = "black"
          ) +
          annotate(
            "text", x = endowment["x"] + 0.62,
            y = endowment["y"] + 0.52,
            label = paste0("w^", agent), parse = TRUE, size = 5.5
          ) +
          annotate(
            "text",
            x = if (agent == "A") 1.3 else 7.5,
            y = if (agent == "A") 5.8 else 3.6,
            label = paste0("U[", agent, "](0)"), parse = TRUE,
            color = panel_colors[agent], size = 5.5
          ) +
          annotate(
            "segment", x = edgeworth1_total_x, xend = edgeworth1_total_x,
            y = 0, yend = -0.2, linewidth = 0.7
          ) +
          annotate(
            "segment", x = 0, xend = -0.2,
            y = edgeworth1_total_y, yend = edgeworth1_total_y,
            linewidth = 0.7
          ) +
          annotate(
            "text", x = edgeworth1_total_x, y = -0.72,
            label = "W[X]", parse = TRUE, size = 5
          ) +
          annotate(
            "text", x = -0.55, y = edgeworth1_total_y,
            label = "W[Y]", parse = TRUE, size = 5, hjust = 1
          ) +
          annotate(
            "text", x = -0.62, y = -0.6, label = agent, size = 6.5
          ) +
          labs(
            x = if (agent == "A") expression(X[A]) else expression(X[B]),
            y = if (agent == "A") expression(Y[A]) else expression(Y[B]),
            title = paste0(agent, "'s diagram")
          ) +
          coord_fixed(
            ratio = 1,
            xlim = c(0, edgeworth1_total_x),
            ylim = c(0, edgeworth1_total_y),
            clip = "off"
          ) +
          edgeworth_theme(base_size = 17, show_axes = TRUE)
      }
    )

    return(panel_plots$A + panel_plots$B)
  }

  additional_tangencies = as.integer(additional_tangencies)
  stopifnot(dplyr::between(additional_tangencies, 0L, 2L))
  show_optimum = show_optimum || show_pareto_set
  additional_tangencies = if (show_pareto_set) {
    max(additional_tangencies, nrow(edgeworth1_trace_points))
  } else {
    additional_tangencies
  }
  show_lens = show_lens || show_optimum

  # Fade the curves introduced at earlier build stages so the newest
  # object stands out on each pause slide
  initial_curve_alpha = if (show_optimum) 0.35 else 1
  optimal_curve_alpha = if (additional_tangencies > 0L) 0.35 else 1

  box_plot = ggplot()
  if (show_lens) {
    box_plot = box_plot +
      geom_ribbon(
        data = edgeworth1_lens,
        aes(x = x, ymin = y_a, ymax = y_b),
        fill = "#8e72a8", alpha = 0.20
      )
  }

  box_plot = box_plot +
    geom_line(
      data = edgeworth1_initial_curves,
      aes(x = x, y = y, color = agent, group = agent),
      linewidth = 1.5, alpha = initial_curve_alpha
    ) +
    annotate(
    "segment", x = edgeworth1_endowment["x"],
    xend = edgeworth1_endowment["x"], y = 0, yend = edgeworth1_total_y,
    linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1.2, color = "grey50"
    ) +
    annotate(
    "segment", x = 0, xend = edgeworth1_total_x,
    y = edgeworth1_endowment["y"], yend = edgeworth1_endowment["y"],
    linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1.2, color = "grey50"
    ) +
    annotate(
    "rect", xmin = 0, xmax = edgeworth1_total_x,
    ymin = 0, ymax = edgeworth1_total_y,
    fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 1.1
    ) +
    annotate(
    "point", x = edgeworth1_endowment["x"], y = edgeworth1_endowment["y"],
    shape = 21, size = 5.5, stroke = 1.5, fill = "white", color = "black"
    ) +
    annotate("text", x = 1.65, y = 6.25, label = "U[A](0)",
             parse = TRUE, color = "#ca5670", size = 6,
             alpha = initial_curve_alpha) +
    annotate("text", x = 7.55, y = 1.7, label = "U[B](0)",
             parse = TRUE, color = "#638ccc", size = 6,
             alpha = initial_curve_alpha)

  if (show_optimum) {
    box_plot = box_plot +
      geom_line(
        data = edgeworth1_optimal_curves,
        aes(x = x, y = y, color = agent, group = agent),
        linewidth = 1.5, alpha = optimal_curve_alpha
      ) +
      annotate(
        "point", x = edgeworth1_optimum["x"], y = edgeworth1_optimum["y"],
        shape = 19, size = 4.5, color = "black"
      ) +
      annotate("text", x = 7.05, y = 3.2, label = "U[A]^'*'",
               parse = TRUE, color = "#ca5670", size = 6,
               alpha = optimal_curve_alpha) +
      annotate("text", x = 5.65, y = 1.45, label = "U[B]^'*'",
               parse = TRUE, color = "#638ccc", size = 6,
               alpha = optimal_curve_alpha)
  }

  if (additional_tangencies > 0L) {
    visible_trace_points = edgeworth1_trace_points |>
      slice_head(n = additional_tangencies)
    visible_trace_curves = edgeworth1_trace_curves |>
      filter(point_id <= additional_tangencies) |>
      mutate(
        arc_alpha = dplyr::if_else(
          !show_pareto_set & point_id == additional_tangencies, 1, 0.35
        )
      )
    box_plot = box_plot +
      geom_line(
        data = visible_trace_curves,
        aes(
          x = x, y = y, color = agent, alpha = arc_alpha,
          group = interaction(agent, point_id)
        ),
        linewidth = 1.25
      ) +
      scale_alpha_identity() +
      geom_point(
        data = visible_trace_points,
        aes(x = x, y = y),
        color = "black", size = 3.8
      )
  }

  if (show_pareto_set) {
    pareto_midpoint = edgeworth1_pareto_set |>
      slice(round(n() / 2))
    box_plot = box_plot +
      geom_line(
        data = edgeworth1_pareto_set,
        aes(x = x, y = y),
        color = "#262626", linewidth = 4.2, lineend = "round"
      ) +
      annotate(
        "point", x = edgeworth1_optimum["x"], y = edgeworth1_optimum["y"],
        shape = 19, size = 4.5, color = "black"
      ) +
      geom_point(
        data = edgeworth1_trace_points,
        aes(x = x, y = y),
        color = "black", size = 3.8
      ) +
      annotate(
        "text", x = 2.6, y = 1.55,
        label = "Pareto set", size = 6, fontface = "bold"
      ) +
      annotate(
        "curve", x = 3.3, y = 1.78,
        xend = pareto_midpoint$x - 0.12,
        yend = pareto_midpoint$y - 0.04,
        curvature = -0.16,
        arrow = grid::arrow(
          length = grid::unit(0.08, "inches"),
          angle = 20,
          type = "open"
        ),
        color = "grey25", linewidth = 0.4
      )
  }

  box_plot +
    annotate("text", x = -0.18, y = -0.18, label = "A", size = 7) +
    annotate("text", x = 10.18, y = 8.18, label = "B", size = 7) +
    annotate("text", x = 3.2, y = -0.38, label = "w[X]^A",
             parse = TRUE, size = 6) +
    annotate("text", x = 8.2, y = 8.38, label = "w[X]^B",
             parse = TRUE, size = 6) +
    annotate("text", x = -0.35, y = 1.2, label = "w[Y]^A",
             parse = TRUE, angle = 90, size = 6) +
    annotate("text", x = 10.35, y = 5.2, label = "w[Y]^B",
             parse = TRUE, angle = 90, size = 6) +
    annotate("text", x = 5.4, y = -0.52, label = "X[A]",
             parse = TRUE, size = 5.5) +
    annotate("text", x = 4.6, y = 8.48, label = "X[B]",
             parse = TRUE, size = 5.5) +
    annotate("text", x = -0.52, y = 4.4, label = "Y[A]",
             parse = TRUE, angle = 90, size = 5.5) +
    annotate("text", x = 10.52, y = 3.6, label = "Y[B]",
             parse = TRUE, angle = 90, size = 5.5) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(A = "#ca5670", B = "#638ccc")) +
    coord_fixed(
      ratio = 1, xlim = c(0, edgeworth1_total_x),
      ylim = c(0, edgeworth1_total_y), clip = "off"
    ) +
    edgeworth_theme()
}

draw_edgeworth_box(show_panels = TRUE)
```

# Why do externalities arise? Edgeworth Box

In a properly functioning market:

- The endowment point is well-established
--

- A and B can trade X and Y to some Pareto improving point
--

- They continue trading until they achieve a Pareto optimal allocation
--

- This allocation lies on the .hi[contract curve]: the line consisting of all Pareto efficient allocations

---

# Why do externalities arise? Edgeworth Box

The contract curve collects every allocation where A's and B's indifference curves are tangent

.hi[Every point on it is Pareto efficient]

<center>
```{r edgeworth2-curve, echo = FALSE, fig.show = 'hide', warning = F, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 5.8}
edgeworth2_total_x = 10
edgeworth2_total_y = 8
edgeworth2_alpha = 0.35
edgeworth2_beta = 0.65
edgeworth2_mrs_weight_a = edgeworth2_alpha / (1 - edgeworth2_alpha)
edgeworth2_mrs_weight_b = edgeworth2_beta / (1 - edgeworth2_beta)

edgeworth2_contract_y = function(x) {
  edgeworth2_mrs_weight_b * x * edgeworth2_total_y /
    (
      edgeworth2_mrs_weight_a * edgeworth2_total_x +
        (edgeworth2_mrs_weight_b - edgeworth2_mrs_weight_a) * x
    )
}
edgeworth2_utility_a = function(x, y) {
  x^edgeworth2_alpha * y^(1 - edgeworth2_alpha)
}
edgeworth2_utility_b = function(x, y) {
  (edgeworth2_total_x - x)^edgeworth2_beta *
    (edgeworth2_total_y - y)^(1 - edgeworth2_beta)
}
edgeworth2_mrs_a = function(x, y) edgeworth2_mrs_weight_a * y / x
edgeworth2_mrs_b = function(x, y) {
  edgeworth2_mrs_weight_b * (edgeworth2_total_y - y) /
    (edgeworth2_total_x - x)
}

edgeworth2_contract_curve = tibble(
  x = seq(0, edgeworth2_total_x, length.out = 1000)
) |>
  mutate(y = edgeworth2_contract_y(x))

# Compute the two initial indifference curves, their improvement lens, and the
# achievable efficient segment for one endowment.
edgeworth2_make_endowment_data = function(endowment) {
  utility_a = edgeworth2_utility_a(endowment["x"], endowment["y"])
  utility_b = edgeworth2_utility_b(endowment["x"], endowment["y"])
  curve_x = seq(0.05, edgeworth2_total_x - 0.05, length.out = 1400)
  y_a = (utility_a / curve_x^edgeworth2_alpha)^(
    1 / (1 - edgeworth2_alpha)
  )
  y_b = edgeworth2_total_y -
    (
      utility_b /
        (edgeworth2_total_x - curve_x)^edgeworth2_beta
    )^(1 / (1 - edgeworth2_beta))
  core_start = uniroot(
    function(x) {
      edgeworth2_utility_a(x, edgeworth2_contract_y(x)) - utility_a
    },
    interval = c(0.001, edgeworth2_total_x - 0.001),
    tol = 1e-12
  )$root
  core_end = uniroot(
    function(x) {
      edgeworth2_utility_b(x, edgeworth2_contract_y(x)) - utility_b
    },
    interval = c(0.001, edgeworth2_total_x - 0.001),
    tol = 1e-12
  )$root

  list(
    endowment = endowment,
    utility_a = utility_a,
    utility_b = utility_b,
    curves = bind_rows(
      tibble(x = curve_x, y = y_a, agent = "A"),
      tibble(x = curve_x, y = y_b, agent = "B")
    ) |>
      filter(dplyr::between(y, 0, edgeworth2_total_y)),
    lens = tibble(x = curve_x, y_a = y_a, y_b = y_b) |>
      filter(
        dplyr::between(y_a, 0, edgeworth2_total_y),
        dplyr::between(y_b, 0, edgeworth2_total_y),
        y_a <= y_b
      ),
    core = tibble(x = seq(core_start, core_end, length.out = 300)) |>
      mutate(y = edgeworth2_contract_y(x)),
    core_start = core_start,
    core_end = core_end
  )
}

edgeworth2_core1 = edgeworth2_make_endowment_data(c(x = 7.4, y = 4.6))
edgeworth2_core2 = edgeworth2_make_endowment_data(c(x = 3, y = 1))

edgeworth2_tangency_x = c(1.5, 3.4, 5, 8.1)
edgeworth2_tangency_points = tibble(x = edgeworth2_tangency_x) |>
  mutate(y = edgeworth2_contract_y(x))
edgeworth2_tangency_arcs = purrr::map_dfr(
  seq_along(edgeworth2_tangency_x),
  function(point_index) {
    point_x = edgeworth2_tangency_x[point_index]
    point_y = edgeworth2_contract_y(point_x)
    utility_a = edgeworth2_utility_a(point_x, point_y)
    utility_b = edgeworth2_utility_b(point_x, point_y)
    arc_x = seq(max(0.05, point_x - 0.7),
                min(edgeworth2_total_x - 0.05, point_x + 0.7),
                length.out = 160)

    bind_rows(
      tibble(
        x = arc_x,
        y = (utility_a / x^edgeworth2_alpha)^(1 / (1 - edgeworth2_alpha)),
        agent = "A", point = point_index
      ),
      tibble(
        x = arc_x,
        y = edgeworth2_total_y -
          (utility_b / (edgeworth2_total_x - x)^edgeworth2_beta)^(
            1 / (1 - edgeworth2_beta)
          ),
        agent = "B", point = point_index
      )
    ) |>
      filter(dplyr::between(y, 0, edgeworth2_total_y))
  }
)

# The contract curve equates the two marginal rates. Each thick segment is
# the subset that makes both people at least as well off as at its endowment.
edgeworth2_check_x = seq(0.01, edgeworth2_total_x - 0.01, length.out = 500)
stopifnot(
  max(abs(
    edgeworth2_mrs_a(edgeworth2_check_x, edgeworth2_contract_y(edgeworth2_check_x)) -
      edgeworth2_mrs_b(edgeworth2_check_x, edgeworth2_contract_y(edgeworth2_check_x))
  )) < 1e-10,
  edgeworth2_core1$core_start < edgeworth2_core1$core_end,
  edgeworth2_core2$core_start < edgeworth2_core2$core_end,
  all(
    edgeworth2_utility_a(edgeworth2_core1$core$x, edgeworth2_core1$core$y) >=
      edgeworth2_core1$utility_a - 1e-8
  ),
  all(
    edgeworth2_utility_b(edgeworth2_core1$core$x, edgeworth2_core1$core$y) >=
      edgeworth2_core1$utility_b - 1e-8
  ),
  all(
    edgeworth2_utility_a(edgeworth2_core2$core$x, edgeworth2_core2$core$y) >=
      edgeworth2_core2$utility_a - 1e-8
  ),
  all(
    edgeworth2_utility_b(edgeworth2_core2$core$x, edgeworth2_core2$core$y) >=
      edgeworth2_core2$utility_b - 1e-8
  )
)

# Draw the common contract curve and add the achievable set for either
# endowment. The first endowment fades when the second is introduced.
draw_contract_curve = function(show_core1 = FALSE, show_core2 = FALSE) {
  show_core1 = show_core1 || show_core2
  fade_core1 = show_core2
  contract_plot = ggplot()

  if (show_core1) {
    contract_plot = contract_plot +
      geom_ribbon(
        data = edgeworth2_core1$lens,
        aes(x = x, ymin = y_a, ymax = y_b),
        fill = if (fade_core1) "grey70" else "#8e72a8",
        alpha = if (fade_core1) 0.16 else 0.20
      )
    if (fade_core1) {
      contract_plot = contract_plot +
        geom_line(
          data = edgeworth2_core1$curves,
          aes(x = x, y = y, group = agent),
          color = "grey68", linewidth = 1.4
        )
    } else {
      contract_plot = contract_plot +
        geom_line(
        data = edgeworth2_core1$curves,
        aes(x = x, y = y, color = agent, group = agent),
        linewidth = 1.4
        )
    }
  }

  if (show_core2) {
    contract_plot = contract_plot +
      geom_ribbon(
        data = edgeworth2_core2$lens,
        aes(x = x, ymin = y_a, ymax = y_b),
        fill = "#8e72a8", alpha = 0.20
      ) +
      geom_line(
        data = edgeworth2_core2$curves,
        aes(x = x, y = y, color = agent, group = agent),
        linewidth = 1.4
      )
  }

  contract_plot = contract_plot +
    geom_line(
      data = edgeworth2_contract_curve,
      aes(x = x, y = y),
      color = "black", linewidth = 1.5
    ) +
    geom_line(
      data = edgeworth2_tangency_arcs,
      aes(x = x, y = y, color = agent, group = interaction(agent, point)),
      linewidth = 1.5
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data = edgeworth2_tangency_points,
      aes(x = x, y = y),
      color = "black", size = 3.5
    )

  if (show_core1) {
    contract_plot = contract_plot +
      geom_line(
        data = edgeworth2_core1$core,
        aes(x = x, y = y),
        color = if (fade_core1) "grey48" else "#262626",
        linewidth = 4.2, lineend = "round"
      ) +
      annotate(
        "point",
        x = edgeworth2_core1$endowment["x"],
        y = edgeworth2_core1$endowment["y"],
        shape = 21, size = 5.2, stroke = 1.4, fill = "white",
        color = if (fade_core1) "grey52" else "black"
      ) +
      annotate(
        "text",
        x = edgeworth2_core1$endowment["x"] + 0.25,
        y = edgeworth2_core1$endowment["y"] + 0.3,
        label = "c", fontface = "italic", size = 6,
        color = if (fade_core1) "grey52" else "black"
      )
  }

  if (show_core2) {
    contract_plot = contract_plot +
      geom_line(
        data = edgeworth2_core2$core,
        aes(x = x, y = y),
        color = "#262626", linewidth = 4.2, lineend = "round"
      ) +
      annotate(
        "point",
        x = edgeworth2_core2$endowment["x"],
        y = edgeworth2_core2$endowment["y"],
        shape = 21, size = 5.2, stroke = 1.4,
        fill = "white", color = "black"
      ) +
      annotate(
        "text",
        x = edgeworth2_core2$endowment["x"] + 0.25,
        y = edgeworth2_core2$endowment["y"] + 0.3,
        label = "c'", fontface = "italic", size = 6
      )
  }

  contract_plot +
    annotate(
      "rect", xmin = 0, xmax = edgeworth2_total_x,
      ymin = 0, ymax = edgeworth2_total_y,
      fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 1.1
    ) +
    annotate("text", x = 5.1, y = 7.55, label = "Contract curve", size = 6) +
    annotate(
      "segment", x = 4.75, y = 7.3, xend = 4.3,
      yend = edgeworth2_contract_y(4.3) + 0.08,
      arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(0.11, "inches")),
      linewidth = 0.8
    ) +
    annotate("text", x = -0.17, y = -0.17, label = "A", size = 7) +
    annotate("text", x = 10.17, y = 8.17, label = "B", size = 7) +
    annotate(
      "text", x = 5, y = -0.5, label = "X[A]",
      parse = TRUE, size = 5.5
    ) +
    annotate(
      "text", x = 5, y = 8.5, label = "X[B]",
      parse = TRUE, size = 5.5
    ) +
    annotate(
      "text", x = -0.5, y = 4, label = "Y[A]",
      parse = TRUE, angle = 90, size = 5.5
    ) +
    annotate(
      "text", x = 10.5, y = 4, label = "Y[B]",
      parse = TRUE, angle = 90, size = 5.5
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(A = "#ca5670", B = "#638ccc")) +
    coord_fixed(
      ratio = 1, xlim = c(0, edgeworth2_total_x),
      ylim = c(0, edgeworth2_total_y), clip = "off"
    ) +
    edgeworth_theme(base_size = 17)
}
```

# Why do externalities arise? Edgeworth Box

Now suppose Y is not a private good, but a public good/bad, e.g. smoke

--

This means that A and B consume the .hi[exact same level of Y]

--

Unlike our regular Edgeworth Box, now Y increases for .hi[both] A and B as we move to the top of the slide (before Y increased for B as we moved to the bottom)

--

Suppose that A likes Y, but B does not

--

Suppose both start off with the same quantity of X

---

# Why do externalities arise? Edgeworth Box


.pull-left[
<center>
```{r edgeworth3-endowments, echo = FALSE, fig.show = 'hide', warning = F, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5.8}
edgeworth3_total_x = 12
edgeworth3_total_y = 6
edgeworth3_endowment_x = edgeworth3_total_x / 2
edgeworth3_w1 = c(x = edgeworth3_endowment_x, y = 0)
edgeworth3_w2 = c(x = edgeworth3_endowment_x, y = edgeworth3_total_y)
edgeworth3_weight_a = 4
edgeworth3_weight_b = 4
edgeworth3_public_good_offset = 1

# A values more of the public good. B values the remaining clean-air amount,
# so B's utility falls as the public bad rises. The offset keeps both sets of
# indifference curves well-defined at W1 and W2.
edgeworth3_utility_a = function(x, y) {
  x + edgeworth3_weight_a * log(y + edgeworth3_public_good_offset)
}
edgeworth3_utility_b = function(x, y) {
  edgeworth3_total_x - x + edgeworth3_weight_b * log(
    edgeworth3_total_y - y + edgeworth3_public_good_offset
  )
}
edgeworth3_slope_a = function(y) {
  -(y + edgeworth3_public_good_offset) / edgeworth3_weight_a
}
edgeworth3_slope_b = function(y) {
  -(edgeworth3_total_y - y + edgeworth3_public_good_offset) /
    edgeworth3_weight_b
}

edgeworth3_tangency_y = uniroot(
  function(y) edgeworth3_slope_a(y) - edgeworth3_slope_b(y),
  interval = c(0, edgeworth3_total_y),
  tol = 1e-12
)$root
edgeworth3_price_slope = edgeworth3_slope_a(edgeworth3_tangency_y)
edgeworth3_z1 = c(
  x = unname(
    edgeworth3_w1["x"] +
      (edgeworth3_tangency_y - edgeworth3_w1["y"]) /
        edgeworth3_price_slope
  ),
  y = edgeworth3_tangency_y
)
edgeworth3_z2 = c(
  x = unname(
    edgeworth3_w2["x"] +
      (edgeworth3_tangency_y - edgeworth3_w2["y"]) /
        edgeworth3_price_slope
  ),
  y = edgeworth3_tangency_y
)

# Compute A's and B's indifference curves through a given allocation.
edgeworth3_curve_through = function(point, curve_span = edgeworth3_total_x) {
  utility_a = edgeworth3_utility_a(point["x"], point["y"])
  utility_b = edgeworth3_utility_b(point["x"], point["y"])
  curve_x = sort(unique(c(
    seq(
      max(0.05, point["x"] - curve_span),
      min(edgeworth3_total_x - 0.05, point["x"] + curve_span),
      length.out = 400
    ),
    unname(point["x"])
  )))

  bind_rows(
    tibble(
      x = curve_x,
      y = exp((utility_a - x) / edgeworth3_weight_a) -
        edgeworth3_public_good_offset,
      agent = "A"
    ),
    tibble(
      x = curve_x,
      y = edgeworth3_total_y + edgeworth3_public_good_offset -
        exp(
          (utility_b - edgeworth3_total_x + x) /
            edgeworth3_weight_b
        ),
      agent = "B"
    )
  ) |>
    filter(dplyr::between(y, 0, edgeworth3_total_y))
}

edgeworth3_w1_conflict_curves = edgeworth3_curve_through(edgeworth3_w1)
edgeworth3_w2_conflict_curves = edgeworth3_curve_through(edgeworth3_w2)
edgeworth3_z1_curves = edgeworth3_curve_through(edgeworth3_z1, curve_span = 2.4)
edgeworth3_z2_curves = edgeworth3_curve_through(edgeworth3_z2, curve_span = 2.4)
edgeworth3_w1_price_line = tibble(
  x = seq(
    edgeworth3_w1["x"] +
      (edgeworth3_total_y - edgeworth3_w1["y"]) /
        edgeworth3_price_slope,
    edgeworth3_w1["x"],
    length.out = 250
  ),
  y = edgeworth3_w1["y"] +
    edgeworth3_price_slope * (x - edgeworth3_w1["x"])
)
edgeworth3_w2_price_line = tibble(
  x = seq(
    edgeworth3_w2["x"],
    edgeworth3_w2["x"] +
      (0 - edgeworth3_w2["y"]) / edgeworth3_price_slope,
    length.out = 250
  ),
  y = edgeworth3_w2["y"] +
    edgeworth3_price_slope * (x - edgeworth3_w2["x"])
)

# From either rights assignment, the payment line reaches a tangency that
# strictly improves both people's utility.
edgeworth3_tangency_checks = tibble(
  point = c("Z1", "Z2"),
  slope_a = edgeworth3_slope_a(c(edgeworth3_z1["y"], edgeworth3_z2["y"])),
  slope_b = edgeworth3_slope_b(c(edgeworth3_z1["y"], edgeworth3_z2["y"])),
  slope_price = edgeworth3_price_slope
)
stopifnot(
  edgeworth3_utility_a(edgeworth3_z1["x"], edgeworth3_z1["y"]) >
    edgeworth3_utility_a(edgeworth3_w1["x"], edgeworth3_w1["y"]),
  edgeworth3_utility_b(edgeworth3_z1["x"], edgeworth3_z1["y"]) >
    edgeworth3_utility_b(edgeworth3_w1["x"], edgeworth3_w1["y"]),
  edgeworth3_utility_a(edgeworth3_z2["x"], edgeworth3_z2["y"]) >
    edgeworth3_utility_a(edgeworth3_w2["x"], edgeworth3_w2["y"]),
  edgeworth3_utility_b(edgeworth3_z2["x"], edgeworth3_z2["y"]) >
    edgeworth3_utility_b(edgeworth3_w2["x"], edgeworth3_w2["y"]),
  max(abs(edgeworth3_tangency_checks$slope_a -
    edgeworth3_tangency_checks$slope_b)) < 1e-10,
  max(abs(edgeworth3_tangency_checks$slope_a -
    edgeworth3_tangency_checks$slope_price)) < 1e-10,
  abs(
    edgeworth3_z1["y"] -
      (
        edgeworth3_w1["y"] + edgeworth3_price_slope *
          (edgeworth3_z1["x"] - edgeworth3_w1["x"])
      )
  ) < 1e-10,
  abs(
    edgeworth3_z2["y"] -
      (
        edgeworth3_w2["y"] + edgeworth3_price_slope *
          (edgeworth3_z2["x"] - edgeworth3_w2["x"])
      )
  ) < 1e-10,
  all(
    edgeworth3_w1_conflict_curves |>
      group_by(agent) |>
      summarise(y_range = diff(range(y)), .groups = "drop") |>
      pull(y_range) > 0.5
  ),
  all(
    edgeworth3_w2_conflict_curves |>
      group_by(agent) |>
      summarise(y_range = diff(range(y)), .groups = "drop") |>
      pull(y_range) > 0.5
  )
)

# Draw the public-good bargaining sequence. Once W2 is emphasized, the
# completed W1 bargain remains visible in grey for comparison.
draw_public_good_box = function(
  show_w1_conflict = FALSE,
  show_w1_price = FALSE,
  show_w1_optimum = FALSE,
  emphasize_w2 = FALSE,
  show_w2_conflict = FALSE,
  show_w2_price = FALSE,
  show_w2_optimum = FALSE
) {
  show_w1_price = show_w1_price || show_w1_optimum
  show_w1_conflict = show_w1_conflict || show_w1_price
  show_w2_price = show_w2_price || show_w2_optimum
  show_w2_conflict = show_w2_conflict || show_w2_price
  show_completed_w1 = emphasize_w2
  focus_w1 = show_w1_conflict && !emphasize_w2
  fade_w1_initial = show_w1_optimum || show_completed_w1
  fade_w2_initial = show_w2_optimum

  public_good_plot = ggplot() +
    annotate(
      "rect", xmin = 0, xmax = edgeworth3_total_x,
      ymin = 0, ymax = edgeworth3_total_y,
      fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 1.1
    ) +
    annotate(
      "segment", x = edgeworth3_endowment_x, xend = edgeworth3_endowment_x,
      y = 0, yend = edgeworth3_total_y,
      linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 1.2, color = "grey50"
    )

  if (show_w1_conflict || show_completed_w1) {
    if (fade_w1_initial) {
      public_good_plot = public_good_plot +
        geom_line(
          data = edgeworth3_w1_conflict_curves,
          aes(x = x, y = y, group = agent),
          color = "grey70", linewidth = 1.5
        )
    } else {
      public_good_plot = public_good_plot +
        geom_line(
          data = edgeworth3_w1_conflict_curves,
          aes(x = x, y = y, color = agent, group = agent),
          linewidth = 1.5
        )
    }
  }

  if (show_w1_price || show_completed_w1) {
    public_good_plot = public_good_plot +
      geom_line(
        data = edgeworth3_w1_price_line,
        aes(x = x, y = y),
        color = if (show_completed_w1) "grey70" else "grey35",
        linewidth = 1.5
      )
  }

  if (show_w1_optimum || show_completed_w1) {
    if (show_completed_w1) {
      public_good_plot = public_good_plot +
        geom_line(
          data = edgeworth3_z1_curves,
          aes(x = x, y = y, group = agent),
          color = "grey70", linewidth = 1.5
        )
    } else {
      public_good_plot = public_good_plot +
        geom_line(
          data = edgeworth3_z1_curves,
          aes(x = x, y = y, color = agent, group = agent),
          linewidth = 1.5
        )
    }
    public_good_plot = public_good_plot +
      annotate(
        "point", x = edgeworth3_z1["x"], y = edgeworth3_z1["y"],
        shape = 19, size = 4.2,
        color = if (show_completed_w1) "grey62" else "black"
      ) +
      annotate(
        "text", x = 3.55, y = 2.05, label = "Z1", size = 6,
        color = if (show_completed_w1) "grey62" else "black"
      )
  }

  if (show_w2_conflict) {
    if (fade_w2_initial) {
      public_good_plot = public_good_plot +
        geom_line(
          data = edgeworth3_w2_conflict_curves,
          aes(x = x, y = y, group = agent),
          color = "grey70", linewidth = 1.5
        )
    } else {
      public_good_plot = public_good_plot +
        geom_line(
          data = edgeworth3_w2_conflict_curves,
          aes(x = x, y = y, color = agent, group = agent),
          linewidth = 1.5
        )
    }
  }

  if (show_w2_price) {
    public_good_plot = public_good_plot +
      geom_line(
        data = edgeworth3_w2_price_line,
        aes(x = x, y = y),
        color = "grey35", linewidth = 1.5
      )
  }

  if (show_w2_optimum) {
    public_good_plot = public_good_plot +
      geom_line(
        data = edgeworth3_z2_curves,
        aes(x = x, y = y, color = agent, group = agent),
        linewidth = 1.5
      ) +
      annotate(
        "point", x = edgeworth3_z2["x"], y = edgeworth3_z2["y"],
        shape = 19, size = 4.2, color = "black"
      ) +
      annotate("text", x = 8.4, y = 4.2, label = "Z2", size = 6)
  }

  if (show_w1_conflict || show_completed_w1) {
    if (fade_w1_initial) {
      public_good_plot = public_good_plot +
        annotate(
          "text", x = 1.6, y = 1.2, label = "U[A](W1)",
          parse = TRUE, color = "grey62", size = 5.2
        ) +
        annotate(
          "text", x = 2.6, y = 5.45, label = "U[B](W1)",
          parse = TRUE, color = "grey62", size = 5.2
        )
    } else {
      public_good_plot = public_good_plot +
        annotate(
          "text", x = 1.6, y = 1.2, label = "U[A](W1)",
          parse = TRUE, color = "#ca5670", size = 5.2
        ) +
        annotate(
          "text", x = 2.6, y = 5.45, label = "U[B](W1)",
          parse = TRUE, color = "#638ccc", size = 5.2
        )
    }
  }

  if (show_w2_conflict) {
    if (fade_w2_initial) {
      public_good_plot = public_good_plot +
        annotate(
          "text", x = 10.7, y = 2.25, label = "U[A](W2)",
          parse = TRUE, color = "grey62", size = 5.2
        ) +
        annotate(
          "text", x = 10.2, y = 4.55, label = "U[B](W2)",
          parse = TRUE, color = "grey62", size = 5.2
        )
    } else {
      public_good_plot = public_good_plot +
        annotate(
          "text", x = 10.7, y = 2.25, label = "U[A](W2)",
          parse = TRUE, color = "#ca5670", size = 5.2
        ) +
        annotate(
          "text", x = 10.2, y = 4.55, label = "U[B](W2)",
          parse = TRUE, color = "#638ccc", size = 5.2
        )
    }
  }

  w1_color = if (emphasize_w2) "grey62" else "black"
  w2_color = if (focus_w1) "grey62" else "black"

  public_good_plot +
    annotate(
      "point", x = edgeworth3_w1["x"], y = edgeworth3_w1["y"],
      shape = 21, size = 5.2, stroke = 1.4,
      fill = "white", color = w1_color
    ) +
    annotate(
      "point", x = edgeworth3_w2["x"], y = edgeworth3_w2["y"],
      shape = 21, size = 5.2, stroke = 1.4,
      fill = "white", color = w2_color
    ) +
    annotate("text", x = 6.38, y = 0.3, label = "W1", size = 6,
             color = w1_color) +
    annotate("text", x = 5.58, y = 5.7, label = "W2", size = 6,
             color = w2_color) +
    annotate("text", x = -0.2, y = -0.18, label = "A", size = 7) +
    annotate("text", x = 12.2, y = 6.18, label = "B", size = 7) +
    annotate("text", x = 3, y = -0.36, label = "w[X]^A",
             parse = TRUE, size = 6) +
    annotate("text", x = 9, y = 6.36, label = "w[X]^B",
             parse = TRUE, size = 6) +
    annotate(
      "text", x = 7.6, y = -0.48, label = "X[A]",
      parse = TRUE, size = 5.5
    ) +
    annotate(
      "text", x = 4.4, y = 6.42, label = "X[B]",
      parse = TRUE, size = 5.5
    ) +
    annotate("text", x = -0.48, y = 3.3, label = "Y", size = 5.5) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(A = "#ca5670", B = "#638ccc")) +
    coord_fixed(
      ratio = 1, xlim = c(0, edgeworth3_total_x),
      ylim = c(0, edgeworth3_total_y), clip = "off"
    ) +
    edgeworth_theme()
}

draw_public_good_box()
```

# Why do externalities arise? Edgeworth Box

In the previous example we were able to achieve the Pareto optimum even with a public good / externality

--

Why?

--

1. Property rights were assigned to either A or B

2. Transactions costs were low (didn't have to pay a fee to trade X)

---

# Property rights and externalities

A solution to many externalities is to just assign property rights and let the market do its thing

--

We'll talk about a few ways that we can assign property rights

---

# Transactions costs and externalities

Now suppose there were many non-smokers

--

Even if they were assigned the property rights, it might be hard for them to bargain
  - Takes a lot of time to find something that works for everyone
  - Negotiating over how much X each person gets

--

The costs of bargaining may exceed the benefits and we end up stuck at W2

---

# Transactions costs and externalities

Road noise: drivers implicitly have property rights to make noise around roads

--

Even if you prefer quiet, you cannot negotiate a payment with every loud car that might pass

---

# The free-rider problem

Externalities and public goods/bads often exhibit many of the same features

Both are subject to the .hi[Free-Rider Problem]

> A type of market failure that occurs when those who benefit from resources, public goods (such as public roads or hospitals), or services of a communal nature do not pay for them or under-pay

e.g.

- people don't pay their taxes for publicly-provided services
- non-smokers will wait for others to pay in order to reduce smoke

---

# The provision of public goods

---

# Public goods

How do we efficiently provide public goods?

We know:

- Private goods: PMB = PMC $\leftrightarrow$ SMB = SMC
- Goods with negative externalities: PMB = SMC $\leftrightarrow$ SMB = SMC
- goods with positive externalities: SMB = PMC $\leftrightarrow$ SMB = SMC

--

Suppose we have a public good, e.g. depth of a river for public use

How do we decide the socially efficient depth?


---

# Public goods

Optimal provision is .hi-blue[always] given by: SMB = SMC

What are the SMB and SMC for a public good?

--

Public goods have two defining characteristics:

--

.hi[Non-rival:] one person's use does not reduce the amount available to others

--

.hi[Non-excludable:] it is difficult or costly to prevent nonpayers from using the good

--

.hi[Different roles:] non-rivalry shapes aggregation; non-excludability causes free riding

---

# Optimal provision of public goods

What does this mean?

--

When we count up the SMB, we need to add up .hi-blue[everyone's] PMB:

.hi[Optimality:] $SMB = \sum_i PMB_i =  PMC$

--

If we ignore the fact that public goods are non-rival, we get underprovision of the good

--

e.g. the free market underprovides clean air, national defense, etc

---

# Modeling the provision of public goods

How do we model public goods?

--

First: how do we aggregate marginal benefit or demand curves?

Here's how to think about it:

--

.hi-blue[For private goods:]

--

Private goods are rival, only one person can consume each unit

--

At each price, what is the total quantity that is demanded?

--

At each price, we need to add up quantities

--

Private goods: we add demand curves horizontally

---

# Modeling the provision of public goods


.hi-blue[For public goods:]

--

Public goods are non-rival, multiple people can consume each unit

--

At each quantity, what is the total marginal benefit?

--

At each quantity, we need to add up PMBs/prices

--

Public goods: we add demand curves vertically


---

# Public goods: graphical

.pull-left[
```{r pub-good, echo = FALSE, fig.show = 'hide', warning = F}
pmc <- function(x) x
d_b <- function(x) 12 - x
d_a <- function(x) 10 - x
d_h <- function(x) 6 - x
ggplot() +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = 13, label = "B", size = 8) +
  annotate("text", x = 7.5, y = 1.5, label = "A", size = 8) +
  annotate("text", x = 4, y = 1, label = "H", size = 8) +
  annotate("text", x = 8, y = 11, label = "MC", size = 8) +
  stat_function(fun = pmc, color = "#638ccc", size = 1.5) +
  stat_function(fun = d_b, color = "#AAAAAA", size = 1.5) +
  stat_function(fun = d_a, color = "#AAAAAA", size = 1.5) +
  stat_function(fun = d_h, color = "#AAAAAA", size = 1.5) +
  annotate("segment", x = 0, xend = 16.67, y = 13.33, yend = 13.33, 
           linetype = "dashed", size = 1.5, color = "grey50") +
  annotate("segment", x = 16.67, xend = 16.67, y = 0, yend = 13.33, 
           linetype = "dashed", size = 1.5, color = "grey50") +
  annotate("segment", x = 0, xend = 23.33, y = 16.67, yend = 16.67, 
           linetype = "dashed", size = 1.5, color = "grey50") +
  annotate("segment", x = 23.33, xend = 23.33, y = 0, yend = 16.67, 
           linetype = "dashed", size = 1.5, color = "grey50") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    title = element_text(size = 24),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 24), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 24),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 24), axis.title.y = element_text(size = 24),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#ffffff",colour = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#ffffff",colour = NA),
    axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,13), expand = c(0,0), breaks = scales::breaks_pretty()) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,31), expand = c(0,0), breaks = scales::breaks_pretty()) +
  labs(x = "Quantity",
       y = "Marginal Benefit/Marginal Cost")
  
```

![public good demand curves](`r knitr::fig_chunk("pub-good", "png")`)
]

.pull-right[

3 different groups: boaters (B), anglers (A), and hikers (H)

Each has a different marginal benefit for water depth:
- Boaters: MB = 12-Q
- Anglers: MB = 10-Q
- Hikers: MB = 6-Q
- MC of provision: MC = Q

We assume MB can't go negative

]

.pull-right[

The optimal provision of the public good is where the MC curve crosses the SMB curve

This is across the middle segment

Q = 22 - 2Q $\Rightarrow$ Q = 22/3

The optimal quantity of Q = 22/3 is greater than the quantity any individual group would be willing to purchase

---

# Public goods financing

The socially optimal quantity is greater than the individual privately optimal quantities


--

This means that the MC of provision, MC = 22/3

--

Is this the price the groups pay?

--

.hi[No!] It is greater than any individual group is willing to pay

--

If the government is able to provide the good, how does it finance the cost raising the river depth above zero?

---

# Public goods financing

It can charge each group a constant share of this price

--

What share is everyone charged?

--

.hi[Lindahl pricing:] charge each group equal to their marginal benefit

--

Boaters pay: 14/3  
Anglers pay: 8/3  
Hikers: free

--

Notice that the prices sum to the marginal cost!

--

Since the good is non-rival, this is enough to finance the cost

---

# Public goods financing

What is a key problem with Lindahl pricing?

--

People can lie about which group they're in

--

Anglers might say they're hikers

--

It requires perfect information on behalf of the regulator
